title: Bounded adic precision loss under supported blowups
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete and separated for principal ideals $(\pi)$ and $(\rho)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with $\pi$ and $\rho$ non-zero-divisors. Let $H\subset A$ and $L\subset B$ be finitely generated ideals containing $\pi^e$ and $\rho^e$, respectively, where $e\geq0$. The formal blowup in $H$ is covered by $\operatorname{Spf}\widehat{A[H/s]}$, $s$ running through finite generators of $H$, with completion for $(\pi)$; the ordinary chart ring is that of [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Define the formal blowup in $L$ similarly. Suppose $u,v:A\to B$ are continuous homomorphisms with $u((\pi))B=v((\pi))B=(\rho)$, $u(H)B=v(H)B=L$, and $u(a)-v(a)\in\rho^mB$ for all $a\in A$, where $m>e$. The induced maps from the formal blowup of $B$ in $L$ to that of $A$ in $H$ agree on their reductions modulo $\rho^{m-e}$ (equivalently modulo the extended distinguished ideal to this power). In particular, any continuous automorphism of $A$ preserving $H$ and congruent to the identity modulo $\pi^m$ acts trivially on the blown-up space modulo $\pi^{m-e}$. The assertion holds on charts of Noetherian adic formal schemes, defined as spaces covered by the displayed formal spectra with inverse-limit structure sheaves. Iterating through a fixed finite tower of supported formal blowups loses at most the sum of the exponents of the successive center ideals, whenever the two induced maps identify the successive centers. Empty centers have exponent zero. The bounds are unchanged by flat pullback [def-weil-flat-morphism].

proof.text: Put k=m-e>0 and choose generators s_i of H. For w=u or v, the elements w(s_i) generate L. On ordinary chart rings the localization map A_{s_i} -> B_{w(s_i)} restricts to A[H/s_i] -> B[L/w(s_i)], sending a/s_i to w(a)/w(s_i), by [def-nagata-strict-chart-to-extended-blowup-chart]. The maps are continuous because w((pi))B=(rho), and extend to completions by applying their compatible maps on every power quotient and taking compatible sequences [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power]. The completed charts cover by [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change]. These chart maps glue: on the intersection of target charts s_i,s_j the ratio s_j/s_i is inverted, and both restrictions send it to w(s_j)/w(s_i); the base coefficients and all fractions have the same images. Thus they define the claimed two induced formal morphisms. The localization operation and uniqueness here are [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property].

source.place: Lemma 3.3.3, printed p.23, chart computation; two-map extension written out by Q84. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix s=s_i, t=u(s), t'=v(s). Write t'-t=rho^m b with b in B. In C_0=B[L/t] put q=rho^e/t, which belongs to C_0 because rho^e is in L. The ratio r=t'/t is therefore 1+rho^k bq. In the rho-adic completed chart C it is a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical]. The overlap of the ordinary t and t' charts is obtained by inverting r in C_0 and t/t' in B[L/t']: these localizations are the same ring, since a/t'=(a/t)r^{-1} and a/t=(a/t')(t/t')^{-1} for a in L. This follows inside B_{tt'} from the subalgebra definition [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] and the localization universal property. By [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement] completion gives the formal principal overlap. Since r is a unit, it is the whole t chart. Interchanging u and v gives the whole t' chart. Hence these two formal open subsets of the blowup of B coincide. This proves chart preservation, not merely a comparison on an unspecified intersection.

proof.text:
On this common formal chart, for a in H choose c_a,c_s in B with u(a)-v(a)=rho^m c_a and u(s)-v(s)=rho^m c_s. Direct subtraction in the overlap ring gives
u(a)/u(s)-v(a)/v(s)=rho^k (rho^e/u(s)) (c_a-c_s v(a)/v(s)).
Every factor on the right belongs to the common completed chart: rho^e belongs to L and v(a)/v(s) is a chart generator on the identified v chart. Thus the difference is in rho^k C. For a base coefficient a in A the difference is in rho^m B, hence in rho^k C. By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], coefficients and the fractions a/s generate the ordinary source chart, so its two maps to C/rho^k C agree: sums and products of equal residue classes remain equal. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] every element of its pi-adic completion has, modulo pi^k, an ordinary representative. Both maps carry pi^k into rho^k C, so their maps on the completed source chart also agree modulo rho^k. No cancellation of rho, pi or a potentially zero-divisor generator is used.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.3, printed p.23, chart computation; two-map extension written out by Q84. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For each i, Step 2 identifies the u(s_i) and v(s_i) formal opens of the domain, and both morphisms take that common open into the same s_i chart of the codomain. Step 3 gives equal morphisms on its rho^k reduction. The reductions of these opens cover the reduced domain, by the chart cover of [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change]. The equalities agree on overlaps since they are restrictions of the same two morphisms. A map of locally ringed spaces is a continuous map with a sheaf map, and these data are equal if equal on an open cover: point images agree locally and sections agree by the sheaf uniqueness axiom. Thus the reduced morphisms are equal. The two extended distinguished ideals both equal (rho), as assumed, so this is also equality modulo the specified distinguished ideal to power k. For the automorphism clause, if e=0 then H=A and the blowup is the identity, so the original congruence suffices. If e>=1, m>=2 and u(pi)=pi(1+pi^{m-1}c); the parenthesis is a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical]. Thus u((pi))A=(pi), and taking B=A, rho=pi and v=id gives the claim.

proof.text: For formal schemes, work on common formal affine neighbourhoods of the two images: congruence modulo a positive power already gives the same map on underlying points, so every point has such a neighbourhood. Restrict further to domain formal affine opens. Sections on principal refinements are completed localizations with their canonical restriction maps [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement]. Consequently the coefficient congruences restrict to these charts, and Steps 1--4 give equal maps modulo the asserted power locally. Equality then glues as in Step 4. The supported formal blowup construction itself commutes with formal open restriction by [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change]. Therefore the affine calculation proves precisely the asserted chartwise formal-scheme version, including non-affine intersections by refining them into formal affines.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.3, printed p.23, chart computation; two-map extension written out by Q84. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For a tower with successive bounds e_1,...,e_N, set E_j=sum_{i=1}^j e_i. The induction claim is equality of the two maps at level j modulo the extended distinguished ideal to power m-E_j, whenever m>E_j. At j=0 this is the hypothesis. If m>E_j, the induction hypothesis at j-1 has positive exponent m-E_{j-1}>e_j. The two maps identify the next center ideals by the tower hypothesis. Apply Steps 1--5 with this exponent to obtain m-E_j. This induction uses no additional regularity lemma: the calculation in Steps 1--3 required only that rho^e be in the center, the equality of distinguished ideals and the completed chart models; it did not use cancellation or regularity of chart rings. For an empty center the ideal is the unit ideal, its blowup is the identity [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change], and one takes e_j=0. Length-zero towers give the original congruence. If m<=E_N there is no positive-precision conclusion; exponent zero means the zero quotient ring, hence an empty reduction and a vacuous equality. This states the exact range of the tower bound without an implicit negative ideal power.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.3, printed p.23, chart computation; two-map extension written out by Q84. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For a flat adic pullback with Noetherian formal source and the pulled-back ideal of definition, [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change] identifies each pulled-back formal blowup with the blowup of the extended center, compatibly with successive pullbacks and finite towers. Extending ideals preserves rho^e in L and sends rho^m c to the same product of extended sections; it also preserves w((pi))B=(rho) and w(H)B=L. Thus the same q, r=1+rho^k bq, and displayed fraction difference in Steps 2--3 are their images on the pulled-back charts. All congruences and the induction keep the same exponents. This proves unchanged bounds under flat pullback; it does not assert that an arbitrary ordinary tensor product of complete rings is complete. The formal fibre products and chart rings used are the completed ones in the cited node.
